analysis.title: "Delayed Revenue, Delayed Cash Flow": Morgan Stanley Warns Oracle Data Center Delays Could Crush Its Debt
key_insights: Morgan Stanley credit analysts Lindsay Tyler and Benjamin Guerrero, in "ORCL Credit: Lighthouse in the Fog", say a data center delay also means delayed monetization, delayed proof of concept, delayed revenue and delayed cash flow. Oracle has over $600 billion of future revenue tied to AI data center construction.

Oracle 5Y CDS closed at a record 261bps on Thursday (Oct 8), which implies a more than 20% five-year default probability. Tyler told clients to buy protection a year ago when CDS was about 125bps and warned of 150bps and then 200bps.

Project Lighthouse (Port Washington, Wisconsin, 1.3GW campus, one of two Vantage campuses built for Oracle to lease, four buildings, about 902MW critical IT load, contracted September 2025) has shells going up but lacks grid power. It needs Wisconsin PSC approval for new ATC transmission lines via We Energies (WEC).

The PSC revoked its completeness finding on ATC's application in August, the case was closed, and ATC refiled on a new docket, which restarts the clock. MS sees a material risk that meaningful load is not available until mid-2028, versus Oracle's June guidance of initial delivery in 2H CY27.

WEC said Oracle's S&P downgrade triggered additional collateral, with the current rating already requiring full credit support. Oracle is posting cash to the utility for power it will not receive until 2028.
Power, not construction, is the bottleneck at both Lighthouse and Jupiter, and Oracle (or a subsidiary) appears to be the directly contracted party for power at both.

At Jupiter (New Mexico), Oracle is weighing trucking compressed natural gas to the site until Energy Transfer's rerouted pipeline arrives next year, at roughly four times the price of pipeline gas. Oracle shares fell as much as 6.1% on the headline.

Barclays argued the Jupiter force majeure was credit-neutral because about $30 billion of hardware capex is typically spent 2-3 months before an asset goes live. Tyler concedes a delay could push GPU and infrastructure spending to the right, which could help from a technical supply lens, but gives four reasons this is the wrong frame.
MS reason 1: revenue and cash-flow realization is deferred, extending the period before confirmation that Oracle's investment and backlog translate into financial results.

MS reason 2: delays make the balance-sheet and cash-flow impact lumpier. If multiple halls are construction-ready when power arrives, Oracle faces concentrated GPU capex and lease liabilities. The capex is bunched, not cancelled.

MS reason 3: there is limited visibility into the contractual terms behind Oracle's RPO (over $600 billion). It is unclear whether customers have specified compute delivery timelines or what remedies apply for delays.
MS reason 4: execution-risk overhang could spread to customer behavior and pressure prepayments, an important funding source, by affecting new RPO signings or re-contracting.

Oracle borrowed roughly $43 billion in fiscal 2026 (ended May 31) and expects to raise another $40 billion of debt and equity in the current fiscal year. In "ORCL Credit: New Bookings, Old Bills" (Sept 11), Tyler estimated parent funding needs may require two large bond deals by FY28-end even with about $40bn more customer prepayments.

Lighthouse and Shackelford County, Texas are funded through the ~$38 billion Vantage construction loan, part of about $65 billion of shorter-dated loans for Oracle-tied sites, plus the $14 billion Related Digital (RDMICH) bond backing Michigan. The article puts total site debt at roughly $79 billion.

MS asks whether project delays spill into ORCL CDS hedging and whether execution concerns, higher rates and a growing data-center construction debt pool complicate refinancing Abilene's construction debt into longer-dated paper. Abilene has 6 of 8 buildings delivered.
Abilene's $9.4 billion of construction loans are, per the article's covenant comps, interest-only and all due in 2028. The 10Y Treasury yield hit 5.33% last week, the highest since 2002.

About $33 billion of construction debt, roughly 40% of the total, sits on the two sites where power delays are flagged (Lighthouse and Jupiter), before counting Shackelford. Three of the four bank deals are short-dated loans against 15-19 year leases, which depend on Oracle refinancing in 2028-2032.

Goldman's credit desk said AI single-name CDS volumes are up 400% year over year, with Oracle at the top. The 2056 Oracle bonds trade around 82 cents and yield over 8.3%. CDS is roughly 100bps wider than the December level that was then called Lehman-crisis levels.

Oracle is in talks with Apollo and Goldman to fund a chip purchase through an off-balance-sheet vehicle, joining SpaceX and Broadcom. This adds more Oracle-linked paper competing for the same credit buyers.
MS notes Lighthouse timing is still broadly consistent with Vantage's 2028 full-campus completion target, and stresses its negative view pre-existed the project delays and rests on fundamentals.
Next catalysts named: the PSC's completeness ruling on ATC's refiling, due October 19, and Oracle's fiscal second-quarter results in December.

market_movers.rationale: MS credit analysts hold a negative view on Oracle debt that predates the delays. Power delays at Lighthouse and Jupiter push out revenue and cash flow and bunch capex into the 2028 refinancing window.

sector_views.rationale: Third-party-developed AI infrastructure is not always the bond-like asset class it can appear to be (Goldman TMT desk, quoted). Power delays, short-dated construction loans and a growing DC debt pool raise refinancing risk.

earnings_insights: Oracle fiscal second-quarter results are due in December. The article says to watch for a funding plan.
Oracle's June earnings deck showed a drone shot of the Lighthouse site as evidence of progress. On the September earnings call management described the project as very much on track.

risk_factors: PSC ruling on ATC's refiled transmission application, due October 19, could extend the delay beyond mid-2028.
Customer prepayments, a key funding source, may shrink if customers become less willing to prepay or re-contract.
Limited visibility into lease, financing and RPO contract terms, including delivery deadlines and remedies for delay.
Refinancing risk: Abilene's $9.4 billion of interest-only construction loans are due in 2028, and about $79 billion of Oracle-tied site debt is short-dated against long leases.
Capex bunching if several halls are ready at once when power arrives, concentrating GPU spending and lease liabilities.
Higher rates (10Y at 5.33%) and competition from other Oracle-linked paper, including the Apollo/Goldman chip SPV, for the same credit buyers.
Additional utility collateral posting tied to Oracle's S&P downgrade.
vol_and_positioning: Oracle CDS hedging demand is rising as banks stuck with Oracle-linked construction loans hedge their exposure, as MS predicted a year ago.

tension_points.bull_case: Barclays: delays push roughly $30 billion of hardware capex to the right, so Oracle spends less cash for a while, making the Jupiter force majeure credit-neutral. Tyler concedes a delay could help from a technical supply lens. MS also notes Lighthouse timing is broadly consistent with Vantage's 2028 full-campus completion target.
tension_points.bear_case: MS: delayed revenue and cash flow, lumpier capex and lease liabilities when halls come online together, unclear RPO delivery terms and remedies, and risk to customer prepayments. About $33 billion of site debt sits on delayed sites, and Abilene's $9.4 billion of loans come due in 2028.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A PSC completeness ruling on ATC's refiled application (due October 19) that clears the transmission path, or an Oracle funding plan at fiscal second-quarter results in December, would weaken the bear case. A further slip in the ruling would strengthen it.

theme_stances.key_argument: Delays do not shrink Oracle's capex bill, they push it into the 2028 refinancing window and delay revenue and cash flow.
Execution concerns, higher rates and a growing DC construction debt pool could complicate refinancing of Abilene debt into longer-dated paper.
theme_stances.evidence: growing DC construction debt pool could complicate the eventual refinancing of Abilene debt
